title: Did every group earn more?
hook: Group incomes and group sizes both change. Inspect the weighted mean.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: every group's income rises while the mix shifts toward lower-paid groups.

misconception: Treating everyone got richer, average fell as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: every group's income rises while the mix shifts toward lower-paid groups.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: Group incomes rise 10→12 and 30→32. Their shares change from 20%/80% to 80%/20%. What happens to the pooled mean?

claims.text: The changing mix retains 26→16, while fixed weights retain 26→28. Each group gained 2; the pooled decline comes from shifting weight toward the lower-income group.

claims.text: A group-level improvement and an aggregate decline can coexist. To describe within-group change, use a common population mix; to describe actual aggregate income, retain the changing mix and say what it measures.
